issue.title: Approved-epic launch through sase monitor has never been exercised end to end; add a safe smoke harness
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-kp.12 (epic sase-kp, 'End-to-end monitor exercises') as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP, and filed here by sase-kp.land.

WHAT IS MISSING: epic sase-kp phase sase-kp.9 (commit 44796037a) rerouted approved-epic launches through the new monitor machinery: start_epic_launch_monitor() in src/sase/bead/epic_launch.py starts a monitor with the custom statuses EPIC APPROVED -> EPIC CREATED, reports the monitor id back to the approval surfaces, and keeps the old detached-task launch only as a fallback for when the planner lane cannot be resolved. That path has unit coverage, but it is the one monitor entry point in the whole epic that was never exercised against a real launch.

EVIDENCE: sase-kp.12 was the epic's end-to-end smoke phase and successfully drove every other monitor path with real launched agents -- completion plus follow-up handoff, non-zero exit, timeout enforcement and kill, stop with claim release, and list/show in rich, markdown, JSON, output-only, and follow modes. It could not drive this one. Its note records the reason: no EPIC APPROVED / EPIC CREATED monitor appeared anywhere in monitor history, and the phase could not manufacture one because epic phase workers are forbidden from creating beads. Re-confirmed by sase-kp.land on 2026-08-13: 'sase monitor list --all' returns five monitors, none with the epic-launch statuses.

WHY A HARNESS IS THE WORK: the obstacle is that a genuine exercise needs a real approved epic plan, which means writing to the durable bead store and launching real phase agents. The deliverable is therefore a repeatable, safe way to drive start_epic_launch_monitor() end to end without polluting the bead store or spawning real phase work -- for example a throwaway project or bead store plus a trivial single-phase plan, or a launch-approval fixture that stops after the monitor member is created.

SCOPE: (1) build the harness; (2) use it to assert the real observable behavior -- a monitor member is created for the approved epic, its start status is EPIC APPROVED and its stop status is EPIC CREATED, the approval surface receives the monitor id, and the monitor terminates cleanly; (3) exercise the documented fallback, i.e. an approval whose planner lane cannot be resolved still launches through the detached task path; (4) leave no durable beads, artifacts, or workspace claims behind.

RELATED CONTEXT: the four other defects sase-kp.12 found were all caused by the epic and are being fixed as sase-kp epic work before that epic closes; this one is a coverage gap rather than a defect, which is why it is filed separately.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-kp — the epic that introduced the untested path (phase sase-kp.9 rerouted approved-epic launches through sase monitor start; phase sase-kp.12 proposed this follow-up). Read sase-kp.9's and sase-kp.12's notes before starting.

SERIALIZATION ANALYSIS FOR THIS HARNESS (independent review, 2026-08-13): the project owner asked whether approved epics still launch one at a time after sase-kp.9 moved them onto monitors. They do -- but nothing in the monitor layer is what makes that true, so the harness this bead builds should assert it explicitly.

WHAT ACTUALLY SERIALIZES: epic_plan_launch_lock() (src/sase/bead/cli_work_from_plan_store.py:150), an flock anchored on the project's primary workspace (epic_launch_lock_anchor(), same file:141). work_from_plan_file() enters it at src/sase/bead/cli_work_from_plan.py:104-112 and holds it across _work_from_plan_file_locked() (:249) -- archive, bead creation, graph publication, and the wave-1 agent launch -- so per project the entire launch is one critical section. Both the old detached task and the new monitor run the identical 'sase bead work' command with cwd = the primary workspace (start_epic_launch_monitor passes cwd=resolved_cwd, src/sase/bead/epic_launch.py:153-167; the supervisor runs its child in monitor_cwd, src/sase/monitor/supervise.py:128,175), so the anchor is unchanged and the lock still applies. Monitors themselves do NOT serialize: five approvals from five planner lanes start five supervisors immediately, and all five 'sase bead work' children run concurrently until they queue on that flock.

TWO BURST GAPS WORTH COVERING IN SCOPE ITEM (2):
(1) The queue is bounded at DEFAULT_EPIC_PLAN_LAUNCH_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 900 (cli_work_from_plan_store.py:34). Real monitored launches observed at 4-5 minutes ('sase monitor list --all' shows 4m12s and 5m11s members), so the 4th or 5th epic in a rapid burst can exhaust the 900s wait and die with PlanFileWorkError instead of launching. While queued, the monitor sits at EPIC APPROVED with no output; the epic-launch start passes no idle timeout (idle_timeout_seconds defaults to 0.0), so a queued launch is at least not idle-killed.
(2) Two approvals whose planner artifacts resolve to the SAME lane collide instead of queueing. monitor_blocking_start_for_lane() (src/sase/monitor/store.py:106) makes start_monitor raise MonitorAlreadyRunningError, and start_epic_launch_monitor falls back to the detached task only on MonitorLaneError (epic_launch.py:168), so it propagates. It surfaces AFTER the gate response is committed: execute_gate_selection writes response.json and settles the notification (src/sase/notification_gates/executor.py:221-226) before apply_side_effects runs the launch. The plan therefore ends up approved, no longer re-approvable through the gate ('conflict_already_handled'), and never launched -- recoverable only via the 'sase bead work ...' resume string in the error text. The same path fires when the planner's lane holds a 'lost' (pre-reboot) monitor, which blocks starts by design.

SUGGESTED HARNESS ASSERTIONS: drive two approvals concurrently and assert both epics get beads and agents, one at a time and in order; and drive two same-lane approvals and assert the second queues or falls back rather than hard-failing after its response has already been written.
